must_fix.title: 304 Not Modified drops Vary: Accept-Encoding when Compress wraps ETag, violating RFC 9110 §15.4.5 and the doc claim that ETag works with Compress in either order
must_fix.evidence: In-package probe: Compress(5)(ETag(h)) with Accept-Encoding: gzip gives `200 ... Vary:[Accept-Encoding]`; the same request with If-None-Match set to that ETag gives `304 map[Etag:["79cc...-gzip"]]` with no Vary. Cause: finish() deletes Content-Type (middleware/etag.go:195) before the underlying WriteHeader(304), so compressResponseWriter.WriteHeader (middleware/compress.go:310-333) sees nothing compressible and never adds Vary. RFC 9110 §15.4.5 says a 304 MUST generate the Vary a 200 would have had. No test covers it.

nits: Setting Content-Type after WriteHeader(200) now leads Compress to gzip the body (len=25 with Content-Encoding: gzip), where plain Compress sends identity (len=1); the deferred WriteHeader changes the outer middleware's behaviour.
etagResponseWriter always implements http.Flusher and http.Pusher even when the underlying writer doesn't, unlike wrap_writer.go, which only exposes supported interfaces.
TestETagDocumentedInReadme reads README.md from a unit test, which no other middleware test does.
If-None-Match: * turns a bodiless HEAD 200 (no ETag) into a 304 with no ETag; allowed by the spec but not documented.

report:
I'd hold this PR for one fix. `go test ./...`, `go test -race -count=3 -run ETag ./middleware/`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all pass, the README row and link are in place, and the tests sit next to the middleware in `middleware/etag_test.go`. But a 304 sent with `Compress` wrapping `ETag` is missing a header the RFC requires.

**Must fix: the 304 drops `Vary: Accept-Encoding` when `Compress` wraps `ETag`.** I checked this with a temporary in-package test, since deleted; `git status` is as I found it.

```
compress-outer gzip:     200 map[Content-Encoding:[gzip] Content-Type:[text/html] Etag:["79cc…1a-gzip"] Vary:[Accept-Encoding]] len=38
compress-outer gzip INM: 304 map[Etag:["79cc…1a-gzip"]] len=0
```

- **Why it happens:** `finish` deletes `Content-Type` before calling the underlying `WriteHeader(304)` (`middleware/etag.go:195`). `compressResponseWriter.WriteHeader` (`middleware/compress.go:310-333`) then finds nothing compressible, so it never adds `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.
- **Why it matters:** RFC 9110 §15.4.5 says a 304 MUST carry the `Vary` (along with `ETag`, `Date`, `Cache-Control` and so on) that the 200 would have had. A cache that gets this 304 can no longer tell the gzip and identity variants apart.
- **Docs:** the doc comment says "ETag works with Compress in either order" (`etag.go:36`), and the code doesn't live up to that here. No test covers `Vary` on a 304 behind Compress.

**Nits:**
- **Late `Content-Type` changes Compress behaviour.** If a handler calls `WriteHeader(200)` and then sets `Content-Type`, plain Compress sends identity, but with ETag in between the body goes out gzipped:
  ```
  late CT plain compress: 200 map[Content-Type:[text/html]] len=1
  late CT compress+etag:  200 map[Content-Encoding:[gzip] … Vary:[Accept-Encoding]] len=25
  ```
- **`Flush` and `Push` are always there.** The wrapper always implements `http.Flusher` and `http.Pusher`, even when the writer underneath doesn't. The repo's `wrap_writer.go` only exposes the interfaces the underlying writer supports.
- **Unusual README test.** `TestETagDocumentedInReadme` reads `README.md` from a unit test, which no other middleware test does.
- **`*` with an empty HEAD.** `If-None-Match: *` turns a bodiless HEAD 200 into a 304 with no `ETag`. Allowed by the spec, but not called out in the docs.
